blocks.text: Condo buildings in Surrey City Centre

"Surrey City Centre" is the City of Surrey's official name for the downtown core of Whalley — the City lists it as "City Centre (Whalley)," one of its six communities — but the Fraser Valley board's sub-area for this geography is "Whalley," not "Surrey City Centre"; board reporting carries a "Whalley" sub-area and no "City Centre" sub-area, so listings and stats for the downtown are filed under Whalley.
3 Civic Plaza — 13495 Central Avenue
A 52-storey mixed-use tower by Century Group, completed/opened 2018, sharing the complex with the Civic Hotel and KPU's Civic Plaza campus beside Surrey Central Station.
Evolve Tower (Evolve) — 13308 Central Avenue
A concrete tower by Weststone Group one block west of Surrey Central Station: 36 storeys per listing data, built 2018 per current MLS listings (sub-type Apartment/Condo, Whalley sub-area).
One Central — 13350 Central Avenue

A 44-storey residential tower by Aoyuan International at Central Avenue & 133A Street, built 2023 per current MLS listings (sub-type Apartment/Condo, Whalley sub-area). The 11 townhomes are townhouse-form and are not a second entry.
University District — North Tower, 13428 105 Avenue; South Tower, 10448 University Drive
Each tower is counted once — 2 entries.
The Grand on King George — 10750 135A Street (at King George Boulevard)

A 46-storey condo tower by Allure Ventures with office and commercial space in the podium, completed January 2025 per the developer's own account to an industry source; a commercial listing source records the property at 10745 King George Boulevard / 10750 135A Street, year built 2025.
King George Hub One (Hub One) — 13615 Fraser Highway
A residential condo tower by PCI Developments at King George Station, completed 2021, 130.7 metres tall per the project record. PCI states Hub One and Hub Two together comprise 738 suites.
King George Hub Two (Hub Two) — 13655 Fraser Highway
The companion condo tower, completed 2021, 94.8 metres tall. Unit count: see the combined 738-suite figure at Hub One above.
Plaza One (King George Hub) — 13725 George Junction

A residential condo tower by PCI Developments, completed 2025; a project source records 40 storeys and 439 homes, and PCI records Plaza One and Plaza Two together at 886 suites — the two figures reconcile (439 + 447 = 886) and are stated once here.
Plaza Two (King George Hub) — 13745 George Junction
The companion condo tower, completed 2025; a project source records 43 storeys and 447 homes (see the reconciled combined figure at Plaza One).
Park George — 13778 100 Avenue
Concord Pacific's tower at the King George Station end of 100 Avenue, the second tower of its Park Place community.
Camberley Green (also spelled "Camberly Green") — 10172 141 Street (east Whalley, outside the downtown core)
Listings verify a gated 55+ community of 40 homes, rancher townhouses, strata plan NWS2957. Its building page's "rentals not allowed" line is void since November 24, 2022.
The Breezeway — 13910 101 Avenue (Whalley)
A SINGLE current listing states "1 occupant must be 55+" for a unit in this gated complex.

items.t: The core is the downtown around King George Boulevard, City Parkway and 104 Avenue, inside the larger Whalley community in northwest Surrey; Guildford is east, Newton south, Bridgeview and the Fraser River north, and Scott Road / North Delta west.

Planning frame: the City Centre Plan (approved 2017) designates a high-density mixed-use downtown, and an update underway adds a defined Central Business District, an Entertainment District, and more transit-oriented development around stations; in October 2025 Council endorsed creating an Entertainment District in City Centre.

Transit: Whalley/City Centre is the only Surrey community served by SkyTrain — Surrey's four Expo Line stations (Scott Road, Gateway, Surrey Central and King George) are all in this area — and the R1 King George Blvd RapidBus runs through the core from Newton Exchange to Guildford via Surrey Central and King George stations.

Institutions in the core: SFU Surrey and KPU's Civic Plaza campus, Surrey City Hall, the City Centre Library, Holland Park (the downtown's festival green space) and the Chuck Bailey Recreation Centre (being expanded); Central City mall anchors retail at Surrey Central and King George Hub adds grocery and services at King George Station.

Schools (Ministry-listed names, SD36): A.H.P. Matthew Elementary (13367 97 Ave) and École Kwantlen Park Secondary (10441 132 St, French Immersion and Inter-A). Catchments are address-specific — for the test address 13367 97 Ave the SD36 locator gives A. H. P. Matthew Elementary and Queen Elizabeth Secondary.

Flood/ALR: City Centre is upland, away from Surrey's floodplain lowlands (the Nicomekl/Serpentine coastal floodplain toward Cloverdale and Newton, plus the Little Campbell River area in the south), and the core is outside the ALR. Confirm parcel-level status on the City's COSMOS mapping.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two tower clusters — the Surrey Central / Central Avenue cluster (3 Civic Plaza, Evolve, One Central, University District) and the King George Station cluster (King George Hub's four condo towers, The Grand on King George, Park George) — with mid-rise and townhouse product at the core's edges and older single-detached stock in surrounding Whalley blocks.

items.t: District energy: One Central's project record states the City of Surrey required use of its Neighbourhood Energy Utility, with a central plant in the building's basement serving multiple buildings in the area — a utility-cost line to read in the strata budget of any West Village tower, confirmed per building on the Form B package.

blocks.text: Good to know about Surrey City Centre condos

items.t: Your search has to be filed under "Whalley." Board reporting and MLS sub-area data for downtown Surrey sit under Whalley — a literal "City Centre" sub-area search returns nothing, because no such board sub-area exists, even though the City officially calls the downtown "City Centre (Whalley)."

One project site holds six residential towers with two different tenures. King George Hub's four condo towers (Hub One, Hub Two, Plaza One, Plaza Two — 1,624 condos at full build-out per PCI) stand beside two purpose-built rental towers (The Line, Tether — 771 rental homes per PCI). A listing that says only "King George Hub" has not told you whether the unit can be bought at all.
Two of the core's headline towers carry unit counts that do not agree with themselves. Price per unit and strata-vote math off either figure needs the strata plan, not the brochure.

The CAC era ended mid-2026. Density charges on new City Centre projects switched from Community Amenity Contributions to the Amenity Cost Charge regime on June 15, 2026 — the same date the Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900) was adopted — relevant to presale pricing comparisons between in-stream older projects and new launches, and a date older Surrey guides get wrong.

The plan is changing under the towers. The City Centre Plan update adds a Central Business District and an Entertainment District (Council endorsed the Entertainment District in October 2025), and large multi-phase applications such as Onni's Regency Gardens redevelopment (10520 132 St / 105–105A Ave area, Application No. 7924-0084-00) are in process — construction disruption and amenity upside both follow the plan, street by street.

Stale restriction lines are everywhere in Whalley building data. Because rental-restriction bylaws died province-wide on November 24, 2022 without any bylaw amendment being required, older building pages still showing "rentals not allowed" (Camberley Green's page among them) are describing a void bylaw — the Form B, not the aggregator page, is the document to trust.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Surrey City Centre

items.t: Form B diligence (any strata purchase on this area, including the queued complexes if a unit is bought): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern. In the core's mixed-use towers, read the depreciation report and the commercial-component cost sharing early.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Surrey City Centre

items.t: OCP — Surrey Bylaw 21900 (never 18020 as current): The downtown's own layer is the City Centre Plan (approved 2017; an update underway adds a defined Central Business District, an Entertainment District, and more transit-oriented development around stations).

Zoning — Surrey Zoning Bylaw 12000: governs the core's high-density mixed-use designations and the fringe lots alike. Streamside setbacks sit in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw 12000 and vary by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated for Surrey.

Secondary suites — 40% cap: under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, one secondary suite may be permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit; a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite; and a suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit — the "90 m² cap" sometimes quoted is not current. Relevant to fringe house lots, not tower parcels.
Subdivision + servicing — Bylaw 8830 (1986), verified ledger: Parcel-level standards are confirmed with the City.

Density charges — CAC superseded by ACC (June 15, 2026): City Centre projects seeking bonus density paid Community Amenity Contributions under Surrey's two-tier density-bonus framework; the City states CACs were superseded by its Amenity Cost Charge and bonus density provisions as of June 15, 2026, with the CAC page kept as a historic reference for eligible in-stream applications.

Short-term rentals — $358/yr, with the $350 conflict disclosed: in Surrey, only an owner who lives at the property as their primary residence may host a short-term rental, tenants cannot run one, and a business licence at $358 per year is required first, under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 and the Business License Bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — the core is outside the ALR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

items.t: The density-charge regime changed mid-deal in 2026: CACs were superseded by the Amenity Cost Charge and bonus density provisions as of June 15, 2026, with the old CAC page kept only as a historic reference for eligible in-stream applications — a pro forma built on CAC figures needs re-checking against the ACC regime.

The plan is moving under the parcels: the City Centre Plan update adds a Central Business District and an Entertainment District (Council endorsed the Entertainment District in October 2025), and the City is selecting a partner for a City Centre Arena and Entertainment District — upside and construction disruption both follow the plan, parcel by parcel.

One address, two school answers — both settled, for that address only: 13367 97 Ave sits in A.H.P. Matthew Elementary's own block, yet the completed SD36 locator run for that address returns Queen Elizabeth Secondary (not the in-area Kwantlen Park) at secondary level — a reminder that in-area presence is not catchment.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Surrey City Centre
What a duplex looks like in Surrey City Centre

items.t: The usual duplex form: The core's housing is predominantly condo apartments in high-rise towers near the stations, with mid-rise and townhouse product at the core's edges, and older single-detached stock in surrounding Whalley blocks — standard post-war suburban lots, freehold. Two waves frame the stock: 1970s-era low-rise rental and detached stock outside the core, and post-2000 (accelerating post-2015) concrete tower construction inside it. Much of the 1970s low-rise stock around the core is purpose-built rental, not strata at all.

faq.q: Is "Surrey City Centre" the same as Whalley?
faq.a: City Centre is the downtown core inside the larger Whalley community.

faq.q: King George Hub — which towers can I buy, and which are rental?
faq.a: Buy: Hub One (13615 Fraser Hwy) and Hub Two (13655 Fraser Hwy), 738 suites combined, completed 2021; and Plaza One (13725 George Junction) and Plaza Two (13745 George Junction), 886 suites combined, completed 2025. Rental only: The Line (13639 George Junction, 371 units) and Tether (402 units). The names sit on one project site — confirm the tower on the contract, not the project name.

faq.q: Is a unit in a brand-new tower a resale or a developer sale?
faq.a: It depends on the unit, not the building: Plaza One, Plaza Two, The Grand on King George and Park George all completed in 2025, and a never-occupied unit sold by the developer carries 5% GST (with the Bill C-4 first-time buyer rebate and the Newly Built Home PTT Exemption to check) and, on a presale contract, REDMA's 7-day rescission frame. Establish the seller's status before pricing.

faq.q: Can I rent out a City Centre tower unit?
faq.a: Long-term, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, whatever an older building page says. Short-term rentals are different: in Surrey only an owner-occupier may host, tenants cannot, and a $358-per-year business licence is required first.

faq.q: Is Camberley Green a City Centre 55+ option?
faq.a: A buyer who wants it is shopping Whalley, not City Centre.

faq.q: How many townhouse complexes are counted for Surrey City Centre?
faq.a: One Central's and Park George's townhouse-form units are inside tower strata and count as condos only.

faq.q: Is "Surrey City Centre" the same as Whalley?
faq.a: City Centre is the downtown core inside the larger Whalley community.

faq.q: A One Central listing calls my unit a townhouse — is it a townhouse complex?
faq.a: Your fees, depreciation report and bylaws are the tower's.

faq.q: Can I add a suite inside a duplex on a Whalley block?
faq.a: Surrey's rule applies: One suite in a semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area, never in a coach/garden suite — the "90 m² cap" sometimes quoted is not current. Confirm per lot.

faq.q: Which schools serve a City Centre address?
faq.a: Per exact address — the one documented run (13367 97 Ave) returns A. H. P. Matthew Elementary / Queen Elizabeth Secondary; École Kwantlen Park Secondary is located in-area but is not that address's catchment.
